and took his wife among his women.
And he was despised by everyone,
and grace departed from him,
and fear fell upon him.
And he sat inside the palace,
and did not go out to battle at all.
Now Sultan Malik Shah sent Bursuq {his} servant with an army,
to bring back Qutalmish.
And when he approached the district of Constantinople,
he sent to Nikephoros and demanded of him that he surrender Qutalmish to him.
Nikephoros, however, said:
"It is not in our religion to surrender someone who has taken refuge with us,
even if we all perish.
Rather, behold, he is before you;
if you are able to take him, take him."
Then Qutalmish and Bursuq engaged each other.
And when many of the Turks from both sides were killed,
Bursuq sent to Qutalmish and said to him:
"Why should Turks perish between me and you? Rather, let the two of us alone meet one another,
and whoever defeats his fellow shall rule over them all."
And when Qutalmish agreed with him,
Bursuq used a stratagem:
he clothed one of his servants in his own garments and his armor,
and mounted him on his own special horse,
and sent him out against Qutalmish.
And he himself stood with twenty horsemen,
as one who watches a spectacle.
And when the servant and Qutalmish joined battle,
Qutalmish struck the servant and threw him from his horse,
and dismounted to cut off his head.
Then Bursuq and those who were with him leapt upon him and killed him.
And when Qutalmish was thus killed by deceit,
Bursuq was only able to persuade and bring a few people to the Sultan.
And those remaining, being numerous, attached themselves to Sulayman, the son of Qutalmish,
and they departed from the land of the Romans,
and went and seized cities along the seacoast,
Antartus and Tarsus, in the year 475
475 of the Arabs [1082-1083 AD].
And afterwards that Sulayman also gained control over Antioch.
And in the year 476,
470 {OCR: 476} of the Arabs, Sharaf al-Dawla bar Quraysh took Harran,
and impaled the qadi who had ruled over it.
And in the same year, which is the year 1394
1394 of the Greeks (1083 of our Lord),
on the 23rd
of Elul, Philaretos the Armenian took Edessa from the Turks,
about whom we shall speak shortly after.
